mainTopic: How to write a מזוזה: the blank space above and below, whether the passages are written open or closed, and whether the parchment rules for תפילין and מזוזה are required or only ideal.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a ברייתא. In it, רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's teacher wrote a מזוזה with blank space above and below and with the two passages written open, because they are not next to each other in the תורה. רב ruled like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The גמרא answers that he meant only the blank space, which must be as wide as a scribe's clip. אביי proves this. רב holds that custom cannot be overturned, as his statement about אליהו and חליצה with a סנדל shows. The custom is to write the passages closed. רב נחמן בר יצחק offers another approach: closed is the ideal מצוה, but open is also valid. A ברייתא about turning a worn ספר תורה or תפילין into a מזוזה is brought to support him, but the proof is pushed off. The גמרא then discusses whether the rule that תפילין go on קלף and a מזוזה on דוכסוסטוס is required or only the ideal. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The teacher's מזוזה: blank space and open passages
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends by describing a מזוזה written with blank space above and below and with open passages. The reason given is that the two passages are not next to each other in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would leave a blank space on top and a blank space on the bottom, and he would write the passages as open ones. I asked him: רבי, why? He told me: Because they are not next to each other in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר describes how his teacher wrote a מזוזה and why he wrote the passages open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a ספר תורה, the passages of שמע and והיה אם שמוע are separated as closed passages. But in a מזוזה they are taken from two different places in the תורה, so the teacher treated them as separate and wrote them open. This open style is exactly what the next step will question.

keyTerms.meaning: Blank space left on the parchment
'Open' passages: the next passage starts on a new line
Next to each other, adjacent
Since, because

steps.confusionAlert: 'Open' and 'closed' here do not mean a folded or rolled-up מזוזה. They are terms for how the gap between the two passages is written on the parchment.

phrases.english: And he would make a space above and a space below,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's teacher (רבי מאיר), from the earlier part of this ברייתא.

phrases.english: and he would make its passages open.
I said to him: My teacher, what is the reason?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לִי: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין סְמוּכוֹת מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: He said to me: Since they are not adjacent in the Torah.
phrases.notes: The first passage is דברים 6:4–9 and the second is דברים 11:13–21, so they are far apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun before this part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the teacher's practice, a מזוזה gets blank space above and below, and its passages are written open because they are not adjacent in the תורה.

steps.title: Did רב rule that the passages must be open?
steps.stepSummary: רב rules like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and the גמרא suggests this must refer to writing the passages open.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חננאל said in the name of רב: The הלכה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. Isn't that about the open passages?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רב's ruling and suggests it backs the open style. That would be a problem for the view that writes the passages closed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב sides with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר on everything in this ברייתא, then the passages should be open. That clashes with the practice of רב הונא, רב's own student, who wrote them closed.

keyTerms.meaning: The הלכה follows (this opinion)
Isn't it that...? (introduces a suggested reading)
About, regarding

phrases.english: And Rav Ḥananel says that Rav says:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
What, is it not with regard to the open passages?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's ruling to strengthen the ברייתא's open style.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice (held by רב הונא) of writing the מזוזה passages closed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב ruled like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's ברייתא calls for open passages, so the halacha seems to be open.

steps.title: No, רב was talking about the blank space
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב agreed with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר only about the blank space, not about open passages.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He meant the part about the blank space.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem by narrowing רב's ruling. רב agrees only about leaving space above and below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא taught two things: blank space, and open passages. The answer says רב's ruling covers only the first, so the closed style can still stand.

phrases.english: No, with regard to the space.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's ruling covers everything in the ברייתא, including open passages.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב's ruling covers only the blank space above and below.

steps.title: How much blank space?
steps.stepSummary: Since רב rules that blank space is needed, the גמרא asks how big it must be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the size of the required blank space. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know רב's ruling is about the space, a practical question comes up: how much space counts?

keyTerms.meaning: And how much?

phrases.english: And how much space?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A follow-up to the answer that רב meant the space.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The size of the blank space needed above and below.

steps.title: The space of a scribe's clip
steps.stepSummary: The blank space should be as wide as a scribe's clip. The statement is given in the name of רב מנשיא בר יעקב or רב שמואל בר יעקב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר יעקב said (some say it was רב שמואל בר יעקב): As much as a full scribe's clip.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the measurement for the blank space. It is the width of the clip a scribe uses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of a number, the גמרא uses a familiar object from the scribe's work as the measure. There is a doubt about which sage said it, but the measure itself is the same either way.

keyTerms.meaning: As much as the full size of
A clip used to hold the sheets of parchment
Scribes

phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Ya'akov says,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יַעֲקֹב:
phrases.english: and some say Rav Shmuel bar Ya'akov says:
The space of a full scribes' clip.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The blank space is the width of a full scribe's clip.

steps.title: אביי: of course רב meant the space, because the custom is closed
steps.stepSummary: אביי tells רב יוסף that רב must have meant the space. רב follows custom, and the custom today is to write the passages closed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: Don't you agree that when רב ruled, he meant the space? After all, רב holds that custom counts, and nowadays everyone writes them closed!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives support for the answer in step 3. רב could not have meant open passages, because that would go against the accepted custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gives weight to established custom. Since the common practice is to write the מזוזה passages closed, רב would not have ruled against it. So his 'הלכה כרבי שמעון בן אלעזר' must refer only to the blank space.

keyTerms.meaning: You should hold, you should agree
Custom, accepted practice
Nowadays
Everyone has the practice
'Closed' passages: the next passage continues on the same line after a gap

steps.whatToRemember: רב's 'הלכה כרבי שמעון בן אלעזר' means only that blank space is left above and below (a scribe's clip wide). The passages themselves are written closed, as the custom is.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how custom can decide how we read a sage's ruling, and it supports writing the מזוזה passages closed.

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
And you, do you not hold
that when Rav said it, it was about the space?
But Rav holds that custom counts,
and nowadays the general custom is closed passages!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3 with an argument from custom.
steps.raayaObject: That רב's ruling refers only to the blank space.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's general view that custom counts, together with the widespread custom of writing the passages closed.

steps.title: The source that רב follows custom: אליהו and חליצה (first version)
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes רב כהנא quoting רב: if אליהו comes and permits חליצה with a shoe, we listen. If he forbids a sandal, we do not, because the people already use a sandal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said in the name of רב כהנא in the name of רב: If אליהו comes and says you may do חליצה with a shoe, we listen to him. If he says you may not do חליצה with a sandal, we do not listen, because the people already have the custom of using a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues, backing up his claim from step 6 that רב follows custom. He quotes רב's own words about חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a prophet like אליהו cannot cancel what the people already do, such as using a סנדל for חליצה. He can only add a new permission, like allowing a מנעל. This shows how much weight רב gives to an existing מנהג.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony where a widow removes her brother-in-law's shoe, freeing her from יבום
A closed shoe
A sandal, the footwear traditionally used for חליצה
The people have the custom (an established מנהג)

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement is the proof that רב treats an established מנהג as something that cannot be overturned. The whole argument of step 6 rests on it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה, אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: As רבה said that רב כהנא said that רב said:
If אליהו comes and says
one performs חליצה with a shoe, we listen to him;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹלְצִין בְּסַנְדָּל – אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: one may not perform חליצה with a sandal, we do not listen to him,
since the people are already accustomed to using a sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבָּה, אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for step 6's claim that רב follows custom
steps.raayaObject: That רב treats established custom as binding
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement that even אליהו cannot cancel the custom of doing חליצה with a סנדל

steps.title: The second version of רב's statement about אליהו and חליצה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes the same chain with a change: if אליהו says one may NOT use a shoe, we listen. On the sandal, both versions agree that we do not listen.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said in the name of רב כהנא in the name of רב: If אליהו comes and says you may not do חליצה with a shoe, we listen to him. If he says you may not do חליצה with a sandal, we do not listen, because the people already use a sandal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the same statement of רב. The only change is in the part about the shoe.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version אליהו is allowed to forbid the מנעל, but he still cannot cancel the סנדל. So the two versions argue only about the shoe. Both keep the same rule about custom.

keyTerms.meaning: We listen to him (we follow his ruling)
One may not perform חליצה

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions look almost the same. The only difference is the word אֵין in the shoe part. The sandal part is identical in both.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And רב יוסף said that רב כהנא said that רב said:
If אליהו comes and says
one may not perform חליצה with a shoe, we listen to him;

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חוֹלְצִין בְּסַנְדָּל – אֵין שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ,
phrases.english: one may not perform חליצה with a sandal, we do not listen to him,
since the people are already accustomed to using a sandal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא, אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second version of the same source from step 7
steps.raayaObject: That רב treats established custom as binding
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second version of רב's statement, which also refuses to let אליהו cancel the סנדל

steps.title: Both versions agree on custom, so רב must have meant the space
steps.stepSummary: The two versions differ only on using a shoe from the start. Both agree that custom stands. So רב's ruling like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר must be about the blank space, and the גמרא accepts this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we said: what is the difference between the two versions? Only whether a shoe may be used from the start. So must we not conclude that רב was talking about the space? Yes, conclude this.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי is still speaking to רב יוסף. He shows that both versions agree that custom wins, and so concludes that רב's ruling was about the blank space and not about open passages. The גמרא accepts this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The versions argue only about the מנעל לכתחילה. Neither one lets custom be overturned. Since today's custom is to write the passages סתומות, רב could not have ruled to write them פתוחות. So his ruling must be about the ריוח.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?
From the start; the ideal way, before the fact
Conclude from it (the point is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: רב follows established מנהג, and the custom is to write the passages סתומות. So his ruling like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר refers only to leaving a ריוח.

phrases.english: And we said: what is the difference between them?
Using a shoe from the start is the difference between them.
phrases.notes: On the sandal both versions agree, so the custom stands either way.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not conclude that he was speaking of the space?
phrases.notes: "The space" is the blank space discussed in steps 3 to 5.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the two versions in steps 7 and 8
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's ruling like רבי שמעון בן אלעזר refers to the blank space, not to writing the passages open

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: closed is the ideal, but open is also valid
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says it is a מצוה to write the passages closed, but open ones are acceptable. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר only meant that open is also allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is a מצוה to write them closed. But if one wrote them open, it is fine. And what did רבי שמעון בן אלעזר mean by "open"? That even open is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a different way to resolve the question from step 2. Now רב's ruling can be about open passages without going against the custom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is not saying open passages are required, only that they are also valid. So רב can rule like him and the custom of סתומות still stays as the ideal. This is a different answer from the one in step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: the ideal, preferred way
Open passages (another type of break between sections)
It is fine; it is valid
Even (also allowed)

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a second way to understand רב. The ideal is סתומות, but a מזוזה written פתוחות is still valid.

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: מִצְוָה לַעֲשׂוֹתָן סְתוּמוֹת,
phrases.english: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: It is a mitzva to make them closed,
but if one made them open, it is fine,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאי פְּתוּחוֹת דְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: and what does "open" mean, as רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said?
Even open.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר: מִצְוָה לַעֲשׂוֹתָן סְתוּמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 2's question instead of the space answer of steps 3 to 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's words as permission ("even open"), not a requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר required open passages, which would go against the custom of closed ones
steps.terutzMaskana: Closed is the ideal מצוה. Open is also valid, and that is all רבי שמעון בן אלעזר meant.

steps.title: A ברייתא about worn scrolls seems to support רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a worn ספר תורה or תפילין may not become a מזוזה only because we do not lower holiness. That implies it would otherwise be allowed, even though the layout of the passages differs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say a ברייתא supports him? 'In the same way, a worn-out ספר תורה and worn-out תפילין may not be made into a מזוזה, because we do not lower something from a higher holiness to a lower holiness.' This implies that if we did lower holiness, one could make a מזוזה from them. But why should that work? Here the passages are closed and there they are open!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to support רב נחמן בר יצחק, who said a מזוזה is acceptable even if its passages are not laid out the ideal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives only one reason not to make a מזוזה from a worn ספר תורה: lowering holiness. So the difference in layout (closed in one, open in the other) must not be a reason to disqualify. That shows the layout is not essential, just as רב נחמן בר יצחק said.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him?

keyTerms.term: אֵין מוֹרִידִין מִקְּדוּשָּׁה חֲמוּרָה לִקְדוּשָּׁה קַלָּה
keyTerms.meaning: We do not lower an item from a higher level of holiness to a lower one
A ספר תורה that has worn out
This implies (an inference from what the source says)
Closed / open breaks between passages

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him?
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב נחמן בר יצחק from the last step, who said open passages are also acceptable.

phrases.english: In the same way:
A ספר תורה that wore out
and תפילין that wore out —
one may not make a מזוזה from them,
because we do not lower
from a higher holiness to a lower holiness.
This implies: if we did lower, one could make it.
Why should that be?
Here they are closed and here they are open!
phrases.notes: The passages are laid out differently in a ספר תורה and in a מזוזה, yet the ברייתא doesn't treat that as a problem.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for רב נחמן בר יצחק's answer in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's view that the layout of the passages is not essential
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that forbids making a מזוזה from a worn ספר תורה only because of lowering holiness

steps.title: Maybe the ברייתא means only patching a few lines
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: the ברייתא may only be talking about using a line or two to complete a מזוזה, not making a whole one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it means to complete a מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא might only allow taking a few lines from the worn scroll to finish off a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If only a line or two is borrowed, the layout of the breaks between passages never comes up. So the ברייתא says nothing about whether a whole מזוזה with the wrong layout is acceptable.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (pushing off a proof)
To complete, adding missing lines to a מזוזה

phrases.english: Perhaps it means to complete.
phrases.notes: He means using a line or two from the worn scroll to finish a מזוזה, not making the whole מזוזה from it.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא for רב נחמן בר יצחק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא may be talking only about completing a few lines, where the layout of the passages is not involved.

steps.title: תפילין and מזוזה are written on different kinds of parchment
steps.stepSummary: How could a מזוזה ever be made from תפילין? A הלכה למשה מסיני says תפילין go on קלף and a מזוזה on דוכסוסטוס, each on a different side of the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does it really mean that if we did lower holiness, one could make a מזוזה from them? But a ברייתא teaches: it is a הלכה למשה מסיני that תפילין are written on קלף and a מזוזה on דוכסוסטוס. קלף is written on the flesh side, and דוכסוסטוס on the hair side!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the implication of the ברייתא from step 11. A מזוזה cannot come from תפילין, since each must be written on a different material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implied that, apart from the holiness problem, a מזוזה could be made from תפילין. But a הלכה למשה מסיני gives each item its own layer of the hide and its own side to write on. So תפילין parchment seems to be the wrong material for a מזוזה anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A law given orally to משה at Sinai
The outer layer of the hide, used for תפילין
The inner layer of the hide, used for a מזוזה
On the side that faced the flesh / on the side that had hair

phrases.english: Does it mean that if we lowered, one could make it?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
It is a law given to Moshe at Sinai —
תפילין are written on קלף,
and a מזוזה on דוכסוסטוס;
קלף is written on the flesh side,
דוכסוסטוס on the hair side!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the implication of the ברייתא in step 11 and challenges it from another angle.
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that a מזוזה could be made from worn תפילין if not for lowering holiness
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תפילין and a מזוזה need different materials by הלכה למשה מסיני, so תפילין parchment could never become a valid מזוזה.

steps.title: The parchment rule is only the ideal way
steps.stepSummary: The rule about which parchment to use is למצוה: the best way to do it, but not required.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the parchment rule describes the best way to do the מצוה, but a מזוזה on other parchment is still valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the material is not essential, a מזוזה made from תפילין parchment would be acceptable after the fact. That keeps the implication of the ברייתא working.

keyTerms.meaning: As the ideal way of doing the מצוה, not a requirement

phrases.english: It is for the ideal מצוה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the strength of the rule: it is the ideal, not a requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The parchment rule seemed to be required, which would make a מזוזה on קלף invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The parchment rule is only the best way; a מזוזה on other parchment is still valid.

steps.title: A ברייתא says switching makes it פסול
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that if one switched the parchment, the item is פסול. That sounds like the rule is required, not just ideal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if one switched, it is פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 14 with a ברייתא saying a switch of parchment makes the item פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If switching makes the item invalid, then the parchment rule is not just the ideal. That seems to contradict the answer למצוה.

keyTerms.meaning: He changed (used the wrong parchment or side)
Invalid, not acceptable

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: if one switched, it is invalid?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the parchment rule is only למצוה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says a switch makes the item invalid, which means the rule is required.

steps.title: That ברייתא is about תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that says 'switching is פסול' is talking about תפילין written on the wrong material, not a מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'פסול' ruling is only for תפילין. For a מזוזה, the parchment rule stays just the ideal way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For תפילין the material really matters, so switching makes them פסול. A מזוזה on קלף is still valid, so making a מזוזה from תפילין remains possible.

phrases.english: That is about תפילין!
phrases.notes: He means תפילין written on the material meant for a מזוזה; that is what's invalid.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ברייתא to a specific case (תפילין)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Switching seemed to make both תפילין and a מזוזה invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only תפילין become פסול; for a מזוזה the material is only the ideal way.

steps.title: A ברייתא says switching in either one is פסול
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that switching 'in this or in that' is פסול. That sounds like it covers both תפילין and a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: if one switched, whether in this or in that, it is פסול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges again. 'In this or in that' seems to mean both תפילין and a מזוזה, so a מזוזה on the wrong parchment would also be פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This attacks the answer of step 16, which limited the פסול to תפילין. If a מזוזה is also פסול, then the parchment rule is required for it too.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether in this or in that

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
if one switched, whether in this or in that,
it is invalid!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: שִׁינָּה בֵּין בָּזֶה וּבֵין בְּזֶה פָּסוּל
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only תפילין become פסול by a switch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'In this or in that' seems to include a מזוזה, so a מזוזה is also invalid if switched.

steps.title: Both cases in that ברייתא are about תפילין
steps.stepSummary: 'This' and 'that' are two wrong ways of writing תפילין. One is writing on קלף but on the hair side, and the second continues on the next page.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both this and that are about תפילין. This one is where he wrote them on קלף but on the hair side, and that one...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'this or that' means two kinds of mistakes, both with תפילין. The explanation of the second case continues on the next page.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is read as listing two ways to ruin תפילין, not as talking about תפילין and a מזוזה. So a מזוזה on the wrong parchment is still valid, and the answer למצוה stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

phrases.english: Both this and that are about תפילין,
and this one is where he wrote them
on קלף, on the hair side,
and that one...

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads the ברייתא so both cases are about תפילין
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'This or that' seemed to mean תפילין or a מזוזה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are mistakes in תפילין, so a מזוזה is not made פסול by a switch.
